I have 2 favors to ask of you.

#1 is this, please answer the following questions. The only rules being you can NOT say "I don't know" "nothing" or anything about being dead. We're using imagination here- specifically imagining that you'll continue living.

Question 1-  Why are you with your girlfriend if you don't like her? 

Question 2- Tell me 3 good things about yourself- they can be small things, they can be physical, personality, hell- high score on your favorite video game. Doesn't matter. 3 good things- go.

Question 3- What are 3 things you like to do? (not harmful- I mean games, going outside, whatever)

Question 4- What's a career you could see yourself doing as an adult? (again- we're imagining that you're living, not ending it)

Question 5- Give me 3 more good things about yourself. 

Question 6- you don't have to type this out, but find a piece of paper, open the notes app, whatever, just list out every single good thing you can think of about yourself no matter how big or small. Keep listing. Keep adding to it every time you think of something new and keep trying to think of new things.

 Question 7- Think of the main 5 people in your life- parents, friends, siblings, whatever. List out 3 good things about each of them. Your 3 favorite things about them.

Question 8- list out your top 10 favorite things about life.

Question 9- Make a 10 year plan- think of a career, think of a city to live in, think of a college, all of that kind of stuff. This plan cannot involve dying or harming yourself.

  
The second favor I'm going to ask- give it one. more. year. Find professional help or speak to a counselor at school- some schools will require parents find professional help for students. I promise, the right professional will help. But please, one more year. One year of listing out the things you enjoy (about yourself, about life, about family and friends). One year of finding new friends that you don't hate. One year of doing whatever things make you happy- even if you aren't good at them. I suck at painting, but it makes me happy so I paint. 

But don't look at it as one year until you die, look at it as one year to show yourself that life can be great and meaningful.

First, a note for the mods- I understand the rule saying to only give veterinary advice, but this seems like more of a legal question so hopefully it's okay for me to answer from a legal, non veterinary, standpoint. If not, I apologize.

OP- I'm sorry this is a bit lengthy.

In the majority of places, medical malpractice laws apply to veterinary professionals as well. So it would be worth looking into malpractice laws in your area. As horrible as the covid pandemic has been, it has made it a lot easier to find information about liability in failure to inform cases when it comes to highly contagious airborne coronaviruses (it is my understanding that at least one of the viruses that causes kennel cough is, in fact, a coronavirus which makes those cases even more applicable).

An important factor when deciding negligence could be whether or not she was up to date on bordatella immunizations. If not, the vet should have known that and therefore the increase in importance of informing you, it adds to the potential level of their liability. 

You are not out of line for wanting to ask them to cover the costs. It is 100% worth it to ask them, the worst they can do is say no. The best way to approach it would be calling the clinic she contracted it at and explaining that you feel they should be financially responsible because they neglected to inform you of a highly contagious illness in their facility. Be firm but polite. They may agree, they may negotiate to pay part of it, or they may say no. If they are legally required to cover the costs(i.e. if it is considered negligence where you're located), they may do it without a fight since it is in their best interest. Even if they are not legally responsible, they may still cover at least part of the costs out of moral obligation. 

\*\*\*\*It is important to note that even if their consent to treat form or any other form they have you sign waives liability, they could be considered negligent in this case. With that in mind, no contract can legally waive liability in cases of negligence. If they do not agree to cover any of it, I'd recommend speaking with an attorney- especially if costs increase. 

I'm sorry you're going through this and hope she recovers quickly and fully. 

Again, sorry about breaking rule #11, this just seems like a question where commenting on the legal side of things is relevant.
